label.rationale: He's on Coumadin, and the 03/15 cardiology note covers the front end well: stop warfarin 5 days out (last dose 03/15), INR check the day before, enoxaparin bridge. The post-op side is just "will be addressed after surgery," though, so nobody has said when to restart the warfarin. That needs to come back before the 03/21 knee. The daily aspirin doesn't count here, and the pre-op H&P (03/09), signed consent and CBC from 02/25 (24 days out) are all fine.

documents.author: Courtney T. Williams, MD
documents.text:
CARDIOLOGY PROGRESS NOTE
Date: 03/15/2026
Reason for consult: perioperative management of anticoagulation ahead of planned total knee arthroplasty.

HPI: Patient with atrial fibrillation with prior TIA (CHA2DS2-VASc 3, HAS-BLED 1) maintained on warfarin 5 mg PO daily (INR goal 2-3). No history of major bleeding. Prior TIA without residual deficits; no stroke. Reports good adherence. Denies palpitations or presyncope.

Renal function: creatinine 1.02 mg/dL, estimated CrCl 96 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault).
ECG: sinus rhythm with first-degree AV block.
Echo (2025): LVEF 61%, mild left atrial enlargement.
RCRI: 2. Functional capacity >4 METs.

ASSESSMENT: Acceptable cardiac risk for the planned procedure. Bleeding risk of the procedure considered moderate. Thromboembolic risk moderate; bridging recommended given warfarin therapy.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
  1. Stop warfarin 5 days before surgery (last dose 03/15/2026); check INR the day before surgery with goal <1.5. Bridge with enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC q12h starting 3 days prior, last dose 24 hours pre-op. Post-operative anticoagulation will be addressed after surgery.
  2. Continue home beta-blocker through the perioperative period.
  3. No further cardiac testing required prior to surgery.
  4. Please call with questions.

documents.author: Courtney J. Desai, NP
documents.text:
HISTORY & PHYSICAL - PRE-OP
Date of service: 03/09/2026
Patient: James Nguyen    DOB: 01/02/1964
Planned procedure: total knee arthroplasty (scheduled for 03/21/2026)

CHIEF COMPLAINT: Chronic bilateral knee pain, left worse than right.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: 62-year-old male referred by Orthopedic Surgery for pre-operative evaluation prior to total knee arthroplasty. Radiographs show tricompartmental osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone medial joint space; failed injections, bracing, and NSAIDs. Patient denies recent illness, hospitalizations, or changes in medications over the past month. Functional capacity estimated at >4 METs (does yard work).

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Atrial fibrillation.
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY: Right shoulder arthroscopy 2018.

MEDICATIONS:
  - omeprazole 20 mg PO daily
  - vitamin D3 2000 IU PO daily
  - Aspirin EC 81 mg PO daily
  - Coumadin 5 mg PO daily (INR goal 2-3)
ALLERGIES: Sulfa drugs (hives)

SOCIAL HISTORY: Never smoker; drinks 1-2 glasses of wine weekly. Lives with spouse.
FAMILY HISTORY: Father with MI at 68.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: Negative for cough, dyspnea on exertion, dysuria, chest pain, syncope, melena, palpitations. All other systems reviewed and negative.

PHYSICAL EXAM:
  Vitals 10:05  BP 118/76 mmHg, HR 79, Temp: 97.4F, SpO2 95% RA
  General: Alert, oriented, no acute distress.
  Airway: Mallampati I, full neck range of motion.
  CV: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs.
  Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
  Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended.
  Extremities: No edema.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
  62-year-old male being evaluated prior to total knee arthroplasty. Cardiac risk acceptable for planned surgery.
  1. Total knee arthroplasty scheduled for 03/21/2026 with Orthopedic Surgery.
  2. Pre-operative labs per protocol; results to be reviewed prior to surgery.
  3. Continue home medications except as directed by perioperative instructions.
  4. Risks and benefits of surgery discussed at a high level; formal consent per surgical team.

Electronically signed by Courtney J. Desai on 03/09/2026.
